ctx.x: Did you know any of the musicians personally from New Orleans before you went there? You know, I mean, they're really friendly with them. What did you sort of?

No, I never say I'm by seeing him. I know Joe Watson because every time he'd come, he'd have to be around Joe. And I knew Alfred Williams. He was coming here with me. And I know Tom because Tom used to stay back there with that miles when he'd get off at night when he'd get to the train or in the morning go back to New Orleans. And I didn't know too many, too many fellas. Did you get to know him quickly? Oh, after I got in New Orleans, yeah, I was getting to know him a lot because everyone around there wanted me…
What other bands did you sort of play around with like your son when Tom didn't have a joke? Do you remember any other bands that hired you?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Alfred Williams stayed there a long time. Jim Robinson stayed there a long time. But uh, Alfred left and went to Texas.

ctx.x: How long were you with Tom Alvin? How many years?

I was with Tom for about, let's say five, six years. Matter of fact, I was with him from 1918 up to 1924. 1924. 1924, I got married in 1923. 1924, I left here and went to Baton Rouge with Titt Johnson's off string. He had one of the leading bands outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott out of Natchez, and Williams out of Napoleonville, Donisonville.
What was Bud Scott playing at the time? Which instruments?
